reference_prolog:
/*  Self-contained SWI-Prolog program
    Topic: Ohio eviction service of process; whether "mail" can be a permitted secondary method
    State: Ohio
    Focus year: 2021
*/

/* =========================
   Scenario facts (question)
   ========================= */

scenario_state(ohio).
scenario_focus_year(2021).

% We model a single eviction (forcible entry and detainer) action.
scenario_action(eviction1).
eviction_action(eviction1).

% Question's definition: "secondary methods of service" may be used if the primary method is unsuccessful.
% We encode that in the scenario: the primary method was unsuccessful.
primary_method_unsuccessful(eviction1).

% Helper predicate that succeeds exactly when the scenario's factual statement is satisfied.
scenario_statement :-
    scenario_state(ohio),
    scenario_focus_year(2021),
    scenario_action(Action),
    eviction_action(Action),
    primary_method_unsuccessful(Action),
    !.

/* =========================
   Statute encoding (Ohio Rev Code  1923.06 (2021))
   ========================= */

% --- Service methods recognized in the statute (normalized names) ---

% "Mail" methods
statute_service_method(ordinary_mail).        % 1923.06(C)
statute_service_method(certified_mail).       % 1923.06(E), also 1923.06(F)(2)

% Non-mail methods under division (D)
statute_service_method(personal_tender).      % 1923.06(D)(2)(a)
statute_service_method(leave_with_suitable).  % 1923.06(D)(2)(b)
statute_service_method(posting).              % 1923.06(D)(2)(c)

% Whether a method is "mail" in the ordinary sense.
method_is_mail(ordinary_mail) :- !.
method_is_mail(certified_mail) :- !.
method_is_mail(Method) :-
    statute_service_method(Method),
    fail.

% --- Primary vs secondary under the QUESTION'S definition (not a statutory definition) ---

% Primary methods (modeled as the first-attempt methods in 1923.06(D)(2)(a)-(b)).
primary_service_method(personal_tender) :- !.
primary_service_method(leave_with_suitable) :- !.
primary_service_method(Method) :-
    statute_service_method(Method),
    fail.

% Secondary methods (modeled as methods used/available when primary attempts fail).
% Under 1923.06(D)(2)(c), posting is available only if (a) and (b) cannot be made.
secondary_service_method(posting) :- !.
secondary_service_method(Method) :-
    statute_service_method(Method),
    fail.

% --- Core statutory duties/permissions ---

% 1923.06(C): In an eviction action, the clerk SHALL mail the summons + complaint by ordinary mail.
statute_1923_06_c_requires_ordinary_mail(Action) :-
    eviction_action(Action).

% 1923.06(D)(2)(c): If service cannot be made by (a) personal tender or (b) leaving with a suitable person,
% service may be made by posting.
% We model "primary unsuccessful" as the condition for "cannot be made" for purposes of this question.
statute_1923_06_d2c_posting_permitted_if_primary_unsuccessful(Action) :-
    eviction_action(Action),
    primary_method_unsuccessful(Action).

% 1923.06(G)(2): Service is deemed complete when BOTH ordinary mail (C) AND posting (D)(2)(c) have been made.
% We model that, in the "posting after primary failure" path, ordinary mail is part of the required combination.
statute_1923_06_g2_requires_ordinary_mail_plus_posting_in_posting_path(Action) :-
    statute_1923_06_c_requires_ordinary_mail(Action),
    statute_1923_06_d2c_posting_permitted_if_primary_unsuccessful(Action).

/* =========================
   Legal reasoning for the question
   ========================= */

% A method is "permitted as a secondary method" (per question's definition) if:
%  (1) primary was unsuccessful, AND
%  (2) the statute authorizes/requires that method in the post-failure service path.
secondary_method_permitted_under_statute(Action, posting) :-
    statute_1923_06_d2c_posting_permitted_if_primary_unsuccessful(Action),
    !.
secondary_method_permitted_under_statute(Action, ordinary_mail) :-
    % In the posting path, 1923.06(G)(2) requires ordinary mail + posting;
    % and 1923.06(C) independently requires ordinary mail in eviction actions.
    statute_1923_06_g2_requires_ordinary_mail_plus_posting_in_posting_path(Action),
    !.

% The question: "Is mail a permitted secondary method of service for an eviction action?"
% We answer "yes" if there exists a mail method permitted as secondary in the scenario.
housing_answer(yes) :-
    scenario_statement,
    scenario_action(Action),
    secondary_method_permitted_under_statute(Action, Method),
    method_is_mail(Method),
    !.
housing_answer(no) :-
    !.

/* =========================
   Main entrypoint (required)
   ========================= */

main :-
    housing_answer(Result),
    format('housing_answer(~w).~n', [Result]).


:- initialization(main, main).

expected.question: Secondary methods of service are defined as those methods that may be used if the primary method is unsuccessful. Is mail a permitted secondary method of service for an eviction action?
